head: 00c215b1fcb8a24674f696f43b892b0ecf1ae041
classification_reasons: The overall change (0002) remains a security-authz control (sdlc.yaml risk_list item 'auth') with a large blast radius: a new hook (plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py, ~985 lines) wired onto every Bash/PowerShell call across every phase, a CI sandbox denyWrite layer, and plugin/ci/run_phase.py settings rewriting -- none of that is reopened or touched by this round, but the plan this round belongs to is still the one that carries that radius.

spec.md still carries accepted residual gaps (sandbox live-proof deferred to a follow-up PR, a documented ceiling on what the hook can and cannot close) rather than a fully closed, zero-open-question spec.

Coverage for shell_guard.py comes entirely from tests this same change added, not pre-existing tests; this round's own one-line edit is to a test the change itself introduced (test_the_framework_suite_s_cases_load's literal list), not a pre-existing assertion, so no weakening of an inherited test occurred.
attempted: Intent: this round's only change request on file (review #5488209275, fix-requests.json id 5488209275) is the one-line literal-list edit; checked the round applies exactly that and nothing adjacent -- no scope drift toward the sandbox follow-up, no new hook behavior, no new eval-case content touched.

Spec and plan: plan.md's own text (line 78-81, 'tests/test_evals.py's test_the_framework_suite_s_cases_load literal list (above) gains the sixth folder name ... in the same commit as the eval case') is now literally inaccurate -- the eval case folder was committed in an earlier round (1a6cf117e2) and the literal-list entry is added in this separate, later commit (00c215b) -- but the owner's instruction for this round was explicit and narrow ('Apply the one-line fix ... and nothing else'), so leaving plan.md's prose unrevised is the owner's own scoping choice, not a defect this round introduced; noting it as a pre-existing, already-surfaced, non-blocking drift rather than a reason to escalate.

Proof: evidence/test.log, build.log and lint.log all carry the identical stale timestamp 2026-10-09T11:08:49Z, predating both the owner's iteration-cap reset (2026-10-12T08:29:59Z) and this round's commit, so they prove nothing about this round's edit (consistent with this same gap being flagged, and accepted, by the adversarial review on the immediately preceding round). No fresh verifier.md exists for this phase-(e) round either (the committed verifier.md is scoped to phase (d)). Because the committed logs cannot be trusted for this edit, verified the fix directly against the source instead of the log's claim: read plugin/evals/run.py's discover() (sorted glob of non-hidden directories under evals/cases/, by name) and confirmed via Glob that evals/cases/ on disk contains exactly six folders -- 0001-protected-path-denied, 0002-intent-skill-shape, 0002-security-authz-the-guardrail-self-protec, 0003-secrets-stay-out, 0004-verify-before-done, 0005-hooks-loaded -- in that exact sorted order; read tests/test_evals.py on disk and confirmed test_the_framework_suite_s_cases_load's literal list matches that list exactly, with the new entry placed immediately after "0002-intent-skill-shape" and before "0003-secrets-stay-out" as the owner asked; confirmed the new case folder's checks.yaml/prompt.md exist and are well-formed (same shape as case 0005), so run.load_case should not raise. On this evidence the test is a real, not cosmetic, fix: it now asserts ground truth against the actual folder set rather than failing with an AssertionError (the failure mode the previous round's fresh review reproduced directly).

Blast radius: this round's diff is exactly the one line in tests/test_evals.py (per the commit message, the stated file scope, and the fact that the rest of the cumulative diff's content -- shell_guard.py, hooks.json, settings.ci.json, run_phase.py, docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md, the two manifest version bumps -- was already present and already reviewed in earlier rounds' diffs, with no new hunk for any of those files attributable to this round). No guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) and no risk_list item is newly touched.

Policies: the edit strengthens rather than weakens an assertion (adds a missing, correct literal entry to a list the project deliberately keeps literal per review #5469970014's own reasoning, so a skipped/duplicated case folder is still caught); no security-baseline, data-convention or definition-of-done rule is implicated by a test-only, one-line change.

Tests: checked whether the edit could let a bug pass silently -- it does the opposite (makes a previously-failing assertion pass for the correct reason, matching the on-disk folder set exactly rather than papering over a mismatch); no pre-existing test's behavior-asserting content was altered, only the missing literal added.
